full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J : On an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 20-3-2011 passed by the Joint District Judge and Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No. 224 of 2010 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30- 9-2010 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No. 11 of 2008 decreeing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to his Court may seem fit and proper. 

 On 4-2-2008, the opposite-party as plaintiff filed Title Suit No, 11 of 2008 against the defendant-petitioner in the 4th Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Narayanganj for ejectment of the defendant-petitioner from the suit premises. On 30-9- 2010, the learned Trial Judge, however, decreed the suit holding, inter alia, that the defendant petitioner is a monthly ejectable bharatia. On appeal, the learned Joint District Judge and Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj dismissed the Title Appeal No. 224 of 2010 affirming the judgment and decree of the Trial Court on the score of non-maintainability of the appeal on 20-3-2011. Thereafter the 

 defendant-appellant-petitioner preferred the revisional application and obtained the instant Rule against the impugned judgment and decree dated 20-3-2011. 

 5. Mr MA Qayyum Khan also submits that since the defendant-appellant-petitioner felt aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 30-9-2010 passed by the Court of first instance in Title Suit No.11 of2008, he preferred Title Appeal No. 224 of 2010 and the learned Judge of the Court of Appeal below dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the Trial Court holding that the defendant-appellant-petitioner ought to have preferred a Civil Revision under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act relying on the decisions in the cases of Majid Biswas vs Adiluddin Shaikh, 12 DLR 380 and Faziur Rahim vs Shamsul Huda, 29 DLR 380; but curiously enough, he did not notice the provision of sub-section (2) of section 15 of the Small Cause Courts Act while disposing of the appeal and had he noticed the said provision of law at the time of disposal of the appeal, he would not have come to the finding that the appeal is not maintainable. 

 10. Indisputably, the provisions of sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 15 of the Small Cause Courts Act are not attracted in view of the valuation of the suit to the tune of Taka 48,000. Given this scenario, it is ex-facie clear that the Court of first instance rightly tried the suit as a Title Suit and disposed of the same. The learned Judge of that Court, as I see it, was conscious of the valuation of the suit and accordingly he dealt with the matter as a Title Suit and not as a Small Cause Court suit. As a natural corollary to the decree of the Title Suit, the defendant-appellant-petitioner rightly preferred a Title Appeal being Title Appeal No. 224 or 2010; but it transpires that the learned Judge of the Appellate Court below signally lost sight of the provisions of Sub-sections (2) and (3) of section 15 of the Small Cause Courts Act and without taking those provisions into consideration, he simply relied upon the decisions reported in 12 DLR 380 and 29 DLR 380 (supra) and held that the appeal is not maintainable and a Civil Revision under section 25 of the said Act is required to be filed before the High Court Division. 

 11. In the case of Majid Biswas vs Adiluddin Shaikh reported in 12 DLR 380, it has been held that when a Small Cause Court suit is not tried as such, the trial is not rendered invalid; but it will retain its real character and its decree will not be appealable. If any lower Court entertains any appeal or revision that will be without jurisdiction. 

 15. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 20-3-2011 passed by the Joint District Judge and Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No. 224 of 2010 is set-aside and the appeal is sent back to the Court of Appeal below on remand for fresh hearing in the light of the observations made in the body of this judgment and in accordance with law.
